status: reviewed against exact pinned source; native development probe pending
findings: The pinned keymap binds C-x C-w to filewrite. After filename entry, filewrite checks the resolved destination with stat and calls eyorn only when it already exists.

The confirmation text identifies the existing destination. A negative answer returns before writeout; a positive answer continues through writeout and updates the current buffer filename only after the write succeeds.

E10a types the relative destination, submits the filename prompt with Enter, observes the actual overwrite confirmation, answers n with a literal text action, and checks both existing files remain unchanged. E10b edits the buffer, submits the destination with Enter, answers y literally, then verifies unchanged original bytes and exact overwritten bytes.
safety: synthetic files only under owned workspace; secure mode -S; backups disabled with -n
interaction_encoding: Public v3 key actions accept named keys and Ctrl-letter chords; single-character yes/no replies use literal text. The filename prompt also requires Enter before the overwrite confirmation is shown. The first unsupported key and second missing-Enter attempts are independently preserved in the E10 failure readbacks.
